summary.headline: Emmforce H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 73% to INR92.5 crores, but operating cash flow was negative INR5.9 crores on a receivables build to INR63 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated H1 FY27 revenue was INR92.5 crores (up 73% from INR54 crores) with EBITDA of INR16 crores (17% margin) and PAT of about INR6 crores. Standalone EBITDA margin was about 19.5%, below the company's normal 20-22% range, because costs from the West Asia conflict (freight, raw materials, power, gas) were absorbed rather than passed on. The subsidiary Emmforce Mobility posted revenue of INR14.5 crores (INR8.6 crores external) and a loss of INR2.8 crores, and FY27 consolidated revenue guidance was trimmed to INR185 crores from INR195 crores. Management plans price revisions from 1 December 2026 to restore margins.

segments.name: Emmforce Autotech (standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone H1 revenue about INR84 crores, EBITDA INR16 crores at about 19.5% margin, PAT about INR9 crores. OEM share of revenue rose to 41% in H1 FY27 from 7% in FY26, driven by the INR470 crore US program (about INR60 crores revenue expected this year).

segments.name: Emmforce Mobility (subsidiary, agri and forgings)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue INR14.5 crores (INR8.6 crores external) and loss INR2.8 crores. FY27 revenue estimate cut to about INR20 crores from INR30 crores due to TAFE delays and a staggered monsoon. FY28 target about INR40 crores (about INR25 crores external, INR15 crores internal).

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance cut to INR185 crores (Autotech INR165 crores, Mobility INR20 crores from INR195 crores total); management will try to reach or exceed INR195 crores.
FY27 standalone PAT about INR18 crores and consolidated PAT about INR14 crores; standalone EBITDA of about INR18 crores referenced in Q&A.
FY28 guidance: about INR195 crores revenue from Emmforce Autotech and about INR40 crores from Emmforce Mobility; no PAT guidance given for FY28.
Standalone EBITDA margin to return to 20-22% via price revisions effective from 1 December 2026, with some customers possibly extending to about 15 December.
Emmforce Mobility expected to have no cash loss in H2 FY27, but it will still weigh on consolidated margins this year.
Receivables expected to fall to about INR50 crores by end of FY27.

Proposed merger of Emmforce Automotives (Embross) into Emmforce; details after Board approval, then valuation, shareholder, stock exchange and NCLT approvals. Eligibility to move to main Board by May 2027.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about INR350 crores in total; automotive capacity about INR225 crores. Management says most future growth will come from better use of existing capacity.
Baddi plant now 150,000 sq ft with more than 600 people; includes 1,600-ton forging press, CNC lines, SCADA-controlled heat treatment and an R&D centre.
Management expects the 1,600-ton press to be fully utilised in FY28, which may require expansion; 400-ton press and blade line may be used for automotive parts next year.
Major automotive projects would need capex in the machining line; minor projects can be handled with existing equipment.

Hydraulic gear pump shipments to two new US customers expected to start in Q4 FY27 after first orders in January 2027; a long-term US OEM order worth about INR10.5 crores a year has PPAP samples with the customer and production expected next quarter.
demand_pricing: Standalone base (non-OEM) business is growing about 15-20% per management, though analyst calculations showed the non-OEM base largely flat YoY; management did not reconcile this.
Two US customers testing parts could add about INR10 crores a year; an OEM order pipeline of about INR20 crores is expected for FY28 (management confirmed the analyst's assumption).
Europe: exhibition participation in September 2026; management expects Europe numbers in FY28, with US inquiries also coming in.
TAFE: 2 months lost to labour unrest; FY27 TAFE guidance cut from INR30 crores to INR20 crores; TAFE approved blades but had prior-supplier inventory to use first.

Raw material and freight inflation (tungsten, cobalt, steel, aluminium, copper); freight cost almost doubled. Management said the company did not pass costs to overseas customers in H1 and will request increases, with the amount not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the base business barely growing in H1 and how does H2 look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-OEM business is growing 15-20% and that about INR6 crores of new-program sales in FY26 were a base effect; it gave no precise figures and said business is 'nothing always linear'.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategy for Emmforce Mobility and its FY28 path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Mahindra contract manufacturing was not profitable and has been dropped, so the focus is own-brand plus private label; FY28 target about INR40 crores (INR25 crores external, INR15 crores internal), and management expects no loss at that level, with break-even-plus at INR40 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost increase can be recovered in H2 and why is FY27 standalone PAT guided at only INR18 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify the price increase, citing public-forum constraints, but expects 20-22% EBITDA; it said guidance is conservative due to inventory at a US customer being consumed and said it aims to catch up about INR10 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What are receivable norms and the working capital plan?
qa_highlights.answer: US receivables run about 6 months (6-8 weeks of US warehouse inventory, about 2 months transit, about 2 months payment); other customers pay in 60-90 days; receivables expected near INR50 crores by year end. Of the INR63 crores, about INR40 crores is from the US customer.

qa_highlights.question: Can the merger's revenue and profit contribution be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers in a public forum, saying two POs were received, another price was finalised with the PO expected, and traction is greater than at Emmforce Mobility; numbers will follow after Board approval.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 EBITDA impact from cost inflation versus the TAFE production loss separable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the split ready and offered to share it offline.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on customer price revisions from 1 December 2026; management did not disclose the size of the increase, and OEM contracts may need index-based negotiation.
Negative H1 operating cash flow of INR5.9 crores and receivables of INR63 crores; target of about INR50 crores by year end is unproven.
Emmforce Mobility losses (INR2.8 crores in H1) and the FY28 breakeven at INR40 crores revenue; no FY28 PAT guidance provided.
Concentration on TAFE and the US OEM program; TAFE labour unrest and prior-supplier inventory drawdowns delayed volumes.
Pending merger with Emmforce Automotives (Embross); financials not yet disclosed and approvals (Board, valuation, shareholders, NCLT) remain.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term story and H1 headline growth, but cautious and evasive on specifics: management declined to quantify the price increase, the cost-inflation vs TAFE impact split, the merger financials and FY28 PAT, and repeatedly deferred numbers until POs or LOIs materialise.

But when we actually pursued it and went forward, we realized that working with Mahindra was basically like not making any profit.

growth.why: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance cut to INR185 crores from INR195 crores (Autotech INR165 crores held, Mobility cut to INR20 crores), with the US INR470 crore programme (about INR60 crores this year) and two new US customers from Q4 FY27 as backing, but capex was cut to INR3 crores in H1 and most growth is expected from existing capacity.

oneOffs.what: US OEM programme (INR470 crore) ramp, about INR60 crore revenue expected this year, drove OEM share of standalone revenue up to 41% from 7% in FY26
About INR6 crore of new-program sales in FY26 described by management as a base effect, which flatters the YoY comparison for non-OEM business

quality.why: Consolidated H1 revenue rose 73% (INR54 cr to INR92.5 cr), and the brief attributes the surge to the US OEM programme ramp (OEM share 41% vs 7%), so most of the growth is from a single, concentrated programme that may not recur at the same pace, while the non-OEM base was largely flat per analyst calculations, and management has not reconciled its claim of 15-20% growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin about 19.5% in H1 vs normal 20-22%; price revisions from 1 Dec 2026 (some customers possibly to 15 Dec) target a return to 20-22%, though the size of the increase was not disclosed and Mobility losses still weigh on consolidated margin.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management says most future growth will come from better use of existing INR225 crore automotive capacity; capex fell to INR3 crores in H1 from INR18 crores, and the 1,600-ton press is only expected to be fully utilised in FY28, so expansion is a later, conditional need.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: OEM share rose to 41% of H1 revenue from 7% in FY26 on the INR470 crore US programme (about INR60 crores this year), and two new US customers start shipping in Q4 FY27; offset by TAFE cut from INR30 crores to INR20 crores and non-OEM base growth that analysts found largely flat.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The 1,600-ton press is expected to be fully utilised in FY28 and may need expansion, and a machining line is needed for major automotive projects, but no size, amount or date was given and H1 capex was only INR3 crores.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance was cut to INR185 crores from INR195 crores (Mobility cut to INR20 crores from INR30 crores, TAFE cut to INR20 crores), and management will only try to reach or exceed INR195 crores.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guidance has already been cut once, H1 operating cash flow was negative INR5.9 crores, and receivables of INR63 crores must fall to about INR50 crores by year end; the TAFE labour-unrest delay and freight/raw-material inflation are unresolved, and the cost-recovery split was not disclosed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management mentions 400-ton press and blade line may be used for automotive parts next year, and Mobility is moving to own-brand plus private label, but no named product launch or date was given.

rows.label: US OEM hydraulic gear pump ramp (two new US customers, INR10.5 crore/yr order)
rows.why: First orders in January 2027 and shipments from Q4 FY27 to two new US customers; a long-term US OEM order worth about INR10.5 crores a year has PPAP samples with production expected next quarter, with two US customers adding about INR10 crores a year.

rows.label: FY28 OEM order pipeline of about INR20 crores
rows.why: Management confirmed the analyst's assumption of about INR20 crores OEM order pipeline for FY28, but no POs were quantified in the brief.

rows.label: Merger with Emmforce Automotives (Embross)
rows.when: after Board approval; main Board eligibility May 2027
rows.why: Two POs received and another price finalised, but financials are not disclosed and Board, valuation, shareholder, exchange and NCLT approvals remain before a contribution can be quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term story, the US OEM ramp and the H2 margin recovery through price revisions, but declined to quantify the price increase, the cost-vs-TAFE EBITDA split, merger financials and FY28 PAT; analysts pressed on flat non-OEM base growth, negative operating cash flow
